title: Playbook friction mapping — debrief and action log (DevExp)
content:
Purpose: quick debrief of the two-day friction-mapping lab we ran for the Playbook/Quickstarts surface (focus: Python SDK quickstart, Node sample, and the streaming example). This doc collects observations, rough metrics, immediate quick wins, and proposed experiments. Meant for devexp triage + product/SDK owners to pick up.

Session summary:
- When: 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 (2x 90-min sessions, remote moderated; 5 participants each, developers unfamiliar with Redwood).
- Setup provided: single-page quickstart (README + one-liner curl, Python 3 snippet, short troubleshooting FAQ), VSCode sample workspace, and a sandbox key with a small token budget.
- Goal for participants: get a streaming chat response working, measure time-to-first-success (T1S), and try to call a function/tool from the example.
- Facilitators: Aisha (moderator), Jonas (note taker), Marta (UX observer), Wei (SDK support on-call), Samir (metrics capture).

Top-level quantitative signals (approx):
- Median T1S (first successful model response): 27 minutes (range 12–63m). The fastest used the curl snippet; slowest hit auth/region errors.
- % completing tool call from sample: 40% (4/10). Of those who failed, 60% stalled at YAML/function schema mismatch or import errors in Node sample.
- Confusion spikes: 3 clear spikes (auth, deps, streaming vs non-streaming semantics).

Big friction points (ranked by frequency + severity):
1) Auth & region mismatch (highest severity)
   - Symptoms: devs saw 403/region-not-supported errors or stale-looking env var examples. Several tried RUNNING_TOKEN vs REDWOOD_API_KEY naming confusion.
   - Root cause hypothesis: README examples show REDWOOD_API_KEY in some places, RUN_TOKEN in others (legacy variants lived in examples). Quickstart automation sets sandbox token in a different env var name.
   - Evidence: 6/10 participants needed help locating the right env var and how to scope the sandbox key.
   - Proposed immediate: standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY across all quickstarts and add a 1-line env var sanity check snippet.

2) Streaming semantics mismatch
   - Symptoms: devs assumed JSON lines; some attempted to parse as full JSON and threw errors. Others didn't handle partial events and dropped streaming entirely.
   - Root cause hypothesis: examples use two different patterns (websocket vs server-sent events) across samples; docs don't explicitly list tradeoffs.
   - Proposed immediate: add a short sidebar in streaming README showing the 3 recommended patterns (requests library approach, SSE, websockets) and a minimal parsing snippet for each.

3) Node sample dependency/packaging details
   - Symptoms: yarn vs npm mismatch, missing top-level "type":"module" in sample, and failing function imports.
   - Root cause: repo has multiple legacy Node samples with different packaging. Starter template mixed CJS/ESM.
   - Proposed immediate: consolidate to one Node starter (ESM), add 'npm init' quick command and a one-liner to switch if user is on older Node.

4) Function schema and example mismatch
   - Symptoms: tool-calling failures when function signature in sample didn't match the function registry expected by the runtime.
   - Root cause: small drift between Playbook function section and the runtime shim used in sandbox.
   - Proposed: add an automated check in the Playbook CI that validates function signatures against a local shim (ticket ENG-1342 created).

5) Quickstart fragmentation (too many entry points)
   - Symptoms: participants opened multiple READMEs, got overwhelmed choosing between "Quickstart", "Advanced Quickstart", and "Playground".
   - Proposed: collapse to 'Fast path' + 'Power user' sections on the main page and hide advanced paths behind a "Next steps" anchor.

Short anecdotal quotes to preserve context (verbatim-ish):
- "I gave up on streaming because the parser kept throwing and there was no single example I could copy-paste." – participant 3
- "Why are there three different env vars for the same token?" – participant 1
- "I expected the sample to say ‘I will install deps’ and not force me to guess whether to use yarn or npm." – participant 8

Heatmap/flow notes (sketch):
- Entry: README -> choose language (Python vs Node) -> auth -> install deps -> run example -> streaming -> tool call.
- Heatmap: auth (high), install (medium-high), streaming (high), function wiring (medium).

Immediate quick wins (can be done this sprint):
- [A1] Standardize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY across repo and update all READMEs (owner: Jonas). Acceptance: README + one-liner env check added; sample passes auth-check script. PR#4821 links updated.
- [A2] Add a tiny "sanity check" shell command near the top of quickstart that calls /v1/ping or similar to verify token & region (owner: Wei). Acceptance: median T1S target improves by 25% in next lab.
- [A3] Consolidate Node starter to ESM + add explicit 'npm install' one-liner (owner: Marta). Acceptance: Node sample installs cleanly in CI across Node 18/20.
- [A4] Streaming cookboook sidebar & parsing snippet for Python/Node (owner: Aisha). Acceptance: participants can copy-paste parsing snippet and handle partial events.

Medium experiments (2–6 week work):
- [B1] Playbook CI tool-signature validation (ENG-1342) – blocks are infra for running shim in CI, need SRE input.
- [B2] Small onboarding CLI that scaffolds a minimal folder with env file and recommended package.json; aim to reduce T1S by guiding through setup (owner: Samir + SDK). MVP = 2 commands.
- [B3] Telemetry probe: add an onboarding metric in Playbook that emits anonymized events: created_env, installed_deps, first_request_success. This will require privacy review.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should we standardize the env var across all products and internal docs (we think yes) but must coordinate with privacy/infra teams in case of legacy E2E tests that rely on different names.
- CLI vs README investment: CLI reduces time significantly but increases maintenance. Decision needed from product on long-term invest vs docs-first.
- Telemetry: what is the minimum data we can collect without PII and still know where dropoffs happen? Legal review required.

Blockers
- CI validation for function signatures depends on a dedicated test runner in the Playbook repo (ENG-1342). SRE to advise.
- Sandbox token rotation timing may break the sanity-check script; need infra to expose a stable per-test token for a week-long window.

Decisions made in this session
- Consolidate quickstart landing page into 'Fast path' + 'Next steps' (agreed). Owner: Jonas.
- Use REDWOOD_API_KEY as canonical env var (agreed). Owner: Jonas.
- Build minimal parsing snippets for streaming examples and add them inline (agreed). Owner: Aisha.

Action items (next 7 days):
- Jonas: open PR to change env var and update all README references (A1). Target: 2026-11-25.
- Wei: implement /ping sanity-check and add to quickstart; coordinate with infra for stable endpoint. Target: 2026-11-26.
- Marta: update Node starter to ESM, add install guidance, run against CI matrix. Target: 2026-12-01.
- Samir + SDK: prototype two-command onboarding CLI (scaffold + env-check). Target: 2026-12-08.
- Aisha: draft streaming sidebar content and two copy-paste parsing snippets; put into Playbook as PR for review. Target: 2026-11-29.

Meeting artifacts & follow-ups
- Recording link: internal UX lab recording (posted to Slack thread) — see linked_artifacts for thread id.
- Notes: add a short excerpt to the Playbook board summarizing heatmap and owners.
- Follow-up workshop: schedule an internal playtest on 2026-12-06 to validate quick wins and run 2 new participants through the updated flow.

Misc notes / scratch
- Consider adding a small "I made it!" banner that fires on first successful API response — small dopamine boost and data point if we can safely capture event.
- Keep the advanced streaming patterns out of the main quickstart — keep them behind "advanced" to avoid cognitive load.

If you want the short TL;DR to paste into PR descriptions:
- "We ran a 2-day lab with 10 new devs. Main dropoffs: auth env var confusion, streaming parsing, and Node packaging. Immediate fixes: standardize REDWOOD_API_KEY, add ping sanity-check, consolidate Node starter to ESM, add streaming parsing snippets. Owners and PR targets listed above."

Questions for leadership/PM:
- Prioritize CLI vs docs-only for Q1 scope? (ask product)
- OK to pursue telemetry probe (I will start paperwork with legal if approved)?

Last updated: 2026-11-23 (minor edits after PR link added).
